summary: Expanded discovery covers 65 creative fields, 518 repository queries and 18 model tasks, with primary-source web research across all observed fields. Today’s guides complete earlier screened entries and add newly researched audio, animation, CAD, video, image and 3D workflows. First library coverage is distinguished from an actual new release. Complete software grants were reviewed; model, asset, paid-service and proprietary-host terms remain separate. These are documentation reviews, not installations or hands-on demonstrations. Independent quality evidence remains incomplete for most additions. The collector’s interrupted document phase was recovered from saved search responses without repeating searches; two repository queries failed, one was partial, and 112 were bounded by pagination limits. Search bounds and ecosystem gaps remain explicit. Weekly whole-library review begins October 26 and is not due today.

Covered local generation, transcript editing, agent-assisted cutting and production planning. The JoyAI official model page was revisited; an unchanged already-profiled tool is not repeated as a new discovery.

Expanded into learned DSP export, neural amp inference, audiobook production and live music. ADAC connects differentiable training to real-time processing; author performance claims remain distinct from independent tests.

Researched asset generation, geometric inference and scene reconstruction. Asset Tap documents a cross-platform provider-driven asset pipeline; generated geometry still needs topology, rights and downstream workflow review.
Browser-native creative tools and local web interfaces remain in scope. Khuwari offers local ML inbetweening. A browser UI alone does not establish support for every inference host.

Immersive-web authoring and spatial AI workflows were researched through Meta’s developer material and related scene-generation projects. SDK availability is not a verified end-to-end VR creative demonstration.
Researched browser ML, learned DSP and custom creative pipelines. ml5 supplies artist-oriented ML examples; generic infrastructure or software merely written with AI is not automatically eligible.
Covered editable agent-controlled creative systems and live model interaction. LuminAI documents AI dance interaction, but a reviewed software grant was not established for a new eligible entry.
Searched CAD-to-object and AI craft workflows. ClayScape describes generative-AI/ceramic fabrication research; a paper or exported mesh is not proof of a licensed app or a print-ready design.
Covered editable game scenes, animation and asset generation. Asset Tap and LibreTerrain provide project-specific workflows; required providers, models and engine terms remain separate.

Researched artist-controlled inbetweening and agent-authored timelines. Khuwari explicitly starts from supplied keyframes; AI-authored finished pixels and editable scene operations are treated as different workflows.
Researched digital presenters, facial animation and signing avatars. The Signature BSL project describes a capture/AI proof of concept; complete code-license eligibility remains unresolved.

Relighting and neural-render proxy work supplemented repository searches. Disney’s project page describes interactive/differentiable lighting research; a reviewed released code grant was not established.

Researched spatial audio, neural scene representations and immersive environments. Audible World Models exposes research results but marks its code as coming soon, so it is not counted as available open-source software.

Covered monocular geometry, computational cameras and reconstruction. Metric3D receives a first full guide; current library inclusion is not a claim of a new launch or a calibrated measurement result.

Researched transcript cuts, captioning, voiceover and image refinement. Cutscript’s official documentation supplies a concrete editing workflow; service-dependent AI is distinguished from offline timeline editing.

Covered technical SVG drawing, editable animation and gesture-driven design. HandType’s creator describes a MediaPipe hand-tracking typography tool, but no complete root software license was found in the inspected repository.
Researched hand-tracked letterform control and kinetic typography. HandType remains a license gap; a compelling creative demonstration does not substitute for an open-source grant.

StoryForge’s live documentation describes fiction, screenplay/comic adaptation and world development. Its showcase disables generation, and several interactive products remain previews; those differences are reflected in the guide.
Covered slides, narrative packages and chaptered audiobook output. Text2Audio’s local workflow is documented, with non-commercial F5-TTS weights separated from MIT application code.

Researched semantic photo organization, depth references and restoration. Pik-Fix supplies primary research context; image examples do not establish fidelity or permission to use every model commercially.

Researched model-assisted diagramming and data/media visualization. ml5 and AIiveVR provide primary creative/educational context. Semiotic’s actual license file contains an added approval sentence and is held pending clarification.

Interactive dance, body/sensor-driven art and multisensory installations were searched. LuminAI and Mind Draw Play describe creative systems; availability and complete software grants require their own review.
Live music and interactive generation were researched alongside audio-plugin authoring. Magenta’s official material documents real-time music work; no live performance or latency test was run here.

Covered garment recognition and design-to-pattern research. Design2GarmentCode describes a multimodal sewing-pattern workflow; Pasma’s separate local garment classifier is reviewed for user-correctable visual suggestions.

Researched narration, captioning and signed communication. Text2Audio is relevant to alternate media access, while Signature BSL remains a research/code-availability gap. These are creative workflow observations, not accessibility certification.
Covered Android creative control and mobile browser editing. The AI Image Edit author’s announcement describes a phone-oriented UI; inference still runs on a separate supported GPU host.
Artist-facing ML and inspectable animation workflows were researched. ml5’s examples support learning creative ML; no classroom efficacy claims are inferred.
Researched restoration, searchable photo archives and audio reuse. Pik-Fix gives a primary restoration reference; generated restoration can alter content and is not archival ground truth.

Searched adjacent practices beyond the starter examples, including learned DSP compilation, sensory installations and neural material authoring. A new field does not relax the code-license or concrete-AI-use checks.
HapticGen’s project page describes text-conditioned vibration generation and its research setup. No new complete software-license/installation review was established for a separate haptic tool today.

Covered learned room/audio representations and spatial sound research. Audible World Models still marks code coming soon; acoustic-rendering repositories receive separate license and dependency screening.
Researched agent-directed video, design and narrative preparation. StoryForge distinguishes deliverable reference packages from actual finished video production, which informs the scope of its guide.

Researched typographic motion and editable agent-driven animation. Strike a Chord supplies a primary kinetic-typography paper; a reviewed reusable software release was not established from that paper alone.
LuminAI documents movement improvisation with a virtual partner. Gesture-generation code was screened separately; dance documentation does not by itself establish an open software grant.

Researched smell-conditioned media and AI scent installations. Anemoia Device and Microsoft’s olfaction research are primary findings; no fully reviewed creator-facing open-source release is claimed today.

Covered scene, CAD and terrain generation. ArtiCAD provides a primary assembly-generation paper; agent-assisted terrain authoring adds a directly documented creative workflow without certifying structural correctness.
Searched learned holography and display-oriented scene representations. Current primary publications and institutional records were found, but a separately reviewed software grant remains a gap.

Researched editable character motion, keyframe interpolation and facial/gesture pipelines. Khuwari’s documented keyframe workflow is an adjacent primary finding; it is not treated as a complete puppet-rigging system.
ClayScape and earlier AI-aided sculpture research were checked for ceramic design/fabrication. Research results do not establish a downloadable, licensed app or a tested print process.
Researched AI-directed CAD and geometry workflows. AgentCAD and GenCAD supplied live primary context; new guides distinguish editable CAD concepts from engineering validation.

RustGIS and GeoLibre were researched as mapping interfaces with AI assistance. Their complete software/model grants and reproducible creative workflows were not fully established for a new eligible entry.

Checked a primary image-to-painting robotics project and adjacent AI sculpture work. Robotic actuation or an AI-assisted development process alone is not enough to establish the required creative AI functionality.
Khuwari and ToonComposer’s official project materials supplemented searches. The guide emphasizes artist-authored frames and editable inbetweening; no app was installed or rendered in this review.
Searched audio generation tied to visual scenes and spatial events. Audible World Models offers research demonstrations but no released code yet, which is retained as an availability gap.
Kyutai’s codec explainer supplied technical context, and codec repositories were screened for speech/media use. A released codec is distinguished from an unreleased full dialogue system.

Researched neural-model visualization/sonification and sensor-driven art. AIiveVR is a primary research reference; ordinary sonification without an established AI component is not automatically included.
Mind Draw Play and related EEG creative systems were researched. Biosignal input itself does not prove AI functionality, and a project description is not a complete software license.
NeuMatEx describes neural material authoring with inverse rendering. Its project page exposes paper/results material but no reviewed downloadable software grant, so it remains a gap.
Researched lensless imaging and learned camera reconstruction using university project pages. These remain source-backed research findings, not inferred hardware compatibility or new app releases.
COrigami supplied a primary AI-assisted flat-folding research lead. No complete reviewed creator-tool release was established; mathematical results are not a print/cut workflow guarantee.
LibreTerrain was found through its official documentation and GitLab source. Its local MCP bridge lets an assistant edit terrain graphs, with platform package availability disclosed separately.
Researched neural mosaic practices using an artist’s project page and a CVF art record. Artificial-Art source was found but had no complete root license in the inspected files, so it is held.
Visual Anagrams supplied a primary perceptual-image generation reference. Existing work is not treated as newly released; any separate software/model restrictions still apply.
Researched learned halftoning as an adjacent image-to-mark workflow. The paper supports the research finding, not a verified engraving-machine integration or physical output.

Searched neural brush and robotic-painting workflows. Two GitHub queries in this field failed and a third was partial because its next-page response was unavailable after the interrupted collection; these remain explicit coverage gaps. Supplemental live primary-source search found StrokeDiff brushstroke-generation research and the IIT Jodhpur physical-painting project; neither finding establishes a newly available open-source implementation without a complete code/license review.
Adaptive Color Grading supplies a current primary paper on automated color workflows. It is retained as research context until a complete software release and model terms are verified.
Collage Diffusion’s official project and paper were checked for layer composition and harmonization. This established work is not recycled as a new release.

Researched learned display radiance fields and neural stereo/display representations. The primary paper supports the research finding; hardware display support and an eligible app release remain unverified.

SemanticSplat’s project page was checked for language-aware Gaussian scene representations. Today’s geometric pipelines are assessed individually; a semantic research result is not a universal scene-editing capability.
Signature BSL and TERP 360 materials were researched for expressive signing avatars. Public demonstrations and awards do not establish a reviewed open-source software grant.

New adaptive field: AI-assisted audio-plugin authoring and compilation of learned DSP. Ruse and ADAC received source/license review; their plugin targets, dependencies and unverified quality checks are explicit.

watchlist.name: Imagination Studio

watchlist.name: Voxatar

watchlist.name: AiPPT
watchlist.reason: The available documentation mixes project code and a commercial service without establishing a reproducible self-hosted implementation for the advertised workflow. Held from today’s additions.

watchlist.name: AcoustiX
watchlist.reason: The reviewed acoustic data-generation path uses simulation/ray tracing. The linked neural AVR workflow was investigated separately; the simulator alone does not satisfy the AI-only scope.

watchlist.name: TinyLuma
watchlist.reason: Despite its AI-image branding, the documented processing uses bilateral filtering, unsharp masking, LUTs and other conventional algorithms. A learned or agent-driven creative operation was not established.
